title: General | Web | Global accessibility requirements | Visa Product Design System

blocks.t: Find general requirements for testing web experiences.

items: Page title (GEN-1)Accurate title (GEN-1-1)Unique title (GEN-1-2)
Language (GEN-2)Lang attribute (GEN-2-1)Lang of parts of page (GEN-2-2)
AT compatible (GEN-3)Support screen readers (GEN-3-1)Alerts read (GEN-3-2)
A11y validator (GEN-4)Use an Automated Testing Tool (GEN-4-1)

blocks.t: An accurate and descriptive page <title> title must be included on every page or view.

items: Inspect the HTML DOM and confirm that a <title> element is present.
Verify that the page title provided is accurate and descriptive of the purpose of the page and content.
Pass: Page title is accurate and descriptive of the page content.
Fail: Page title is not included or page title is inaccurate and/or not descriptive of the page content.

blocks.t: The page title must be unique and conform to a consistent structure among the other pages.

items: Inspect the target page.
Review the html <title> tag.
Verify that the page title is unique and conforms to a consistent structure among the other pages.
Pass: Page title is unique and conforms to a consistent structure among the other pages.
Fail: Page title is not unique and/or it does not conform to a consistent structure among the other pages.

blocks.t: The applicable language must be defined on every page, inside the html tag.

items: Use the Inspect feature in the browser (for example: Chrome F12 dev tools) to open a view of the page HTML code.
Locate the <html> element at the beginning of the HTML DOM.
Confirm that the lang="" attribute is correct for the language of the page content.
Pass: Correct page language is defined.
Fail: Page language is not defined or the incorrect page language is defined.

blocks.t: A lang attribute must be set on every word or phrase that is in a different language than the page’s main language.

items: Locate any words or phrases in the page content that are in a language that is different from the language of the other content in the page.
Use the Inspect feature in the browser (for example: Chrome F12 dev tools) to open a view of the page HTML code and inspect each of these words or phrases.
Confirm that each of these words or phrases is wrapped in a <span> element with a lang="" attribute that is correct for the language of the word or phrase.
Pass: All words or pages which are in a different language than the global lang are marked up with the appropriate language.
Fail: Words or pages which are in a different language than the global lang are not marked up with the appropriate language.
NA: No words or phrases are in a different language from the global language.

blocks.t: All features and functionality made available to users within the web application must be functionally supported with at least one screen reader per supported platform (for example: JAWS for Windows desktop, VoiceOver for MAC iOS, etc.).
Run through all use cases with each supported screen reader, confirming that all features and functionality are fully available to non-sighted users.

items: Pass: All features and functionality are fully available to non-sighted users.
Fail: One or more features or functionality are not fully available to non-sighted users.

blocks.t: When alerts are shown on screen (for example: success, error, or status/informative) they must also be read aloud by each supported screen reader without receiving focus.
Note: Error messages that appear in-line upon leaving a form field are common examples.
Confirm that when alerts are shown on screen (for example: success, error, or status/informative) they are also read aloud by each supported screen reader.

items: Pass: Alerts shown on screen are read aloud by each supported screen reader.
Fail: Alerts shown on screen are not read aloud by each supported screen reader.
NA: No alerts are shown on screen.

blocks.t: When run against the page, the automated validation tool must not report any errors.

items: Run one automated validation tool of your choice against the page and confirm that it reports no errors.
If errors are found, record a FAIL with a FAIL ID for each issue reported by the tool.
Pass: Automated tool returns zero errors.
Fail: Automated tool returns one or more errors.
